questions.q: What is the Law of Reflection regarding light striking a smooth plane mirror?
a: Angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection
Angle of incidence is greater than angle of reflection
Angle of refraction equals angle of incidence
Angle of reflection is always ninety degrees

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the image formed by a plane mirror?
a: Virtual, upright, laterally inverted, and the same size as the object

questions.q: What is refraction of light?
a: The bouncing of light off a rough surface
The absorption of light inside a dense medium
The bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium into another due to a change in its speed
The splitting of white light into constituent colors

questions.q: Snell Law relates the angle of incidence (i) and the angle of refraction (r) to what refractive index property?
a: The focal length of a lens
The mass of the light ray
The refractive index (n) of the medium, where n = sin(i) / sin(r)

questions.q: What is total internal reflection?
a: When light traveling from a denser medium to a less dense medium strikes the boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle and is completely reflected back inside
When light passes straight through a vacuum without bending
When light is completely absorbed by a black surface
When light reflects off a rough wall diffusely

questions.q: What is the critical angle of a transparent medium?
a: The angle of incidence that produces an angle of refraction of zero
The angle of incidence in the denser medium for which the angle of refraction in the less dense medium is ninety degrees
The angle at which light stops traveling
The angle of reflection off a glass prism

questions.q: An object is placed at a distance greater than twice the focal length (2F) in front of a converging lens. What is the nature of the image formed?
a: Real, inverted, and diminished (smaller than the object)

It passes straight through without bending.
It undergoes total internal reflection, reflecting entirely back into the water.

a: Light rays from the bottom of the pool bend away from the normal as they pass from water into air, making the apparent image appear higher than it is.
The pool floor is made of mirrors.
Water pressure pushes the bottom upward.

questions.q: What medical condition is corrected by using converging (convex) lenses in eyeglasses?
a: Long-sightedness (hypermetropia), where close objects appear blurred because images form behind the retina

questions.q: What is lateral inversion in a plane mirror image?

Left and right appear reversed in the mirror image compared to the object.
The image is pushed backward into the wall.
Colors of the object are inverted.

a: Magnification = Focal length divided by lens diameter
Magnification = 1 + (D / f), where D is the least distance of distinct vision and f is focal length

questions.q: Why does a diamond sparkle brilliantly with many colored flashes of light when cut properly?
a: Diamond has a very high refractive index (about 2.42) and a very small critical angle (about 24.5 degrees), causing intense internal reflection and strong dispersion.

questions.q: When a ray of light passes perpendicularly (at an angle of incidence of 0 degrees) from air into a glass block, what happens to its path and speed?
a: Its speed decreases, but it continues straight ahead without any change in direction (no refraction).

questions.q: What type of image is always produced by a concave (diverging) lens, regardless of where the real object is placed?
